IOHN.|253}}</noinclude>therfore vvalked no more openly among the Ievves, but he vvent into the countrie beside the desert vnto a citie that is called Ephrem, and there he abode vvith his Disciples.⊣ {{verse|chapter=11|verse=55}}† And the Pasche of the Ievves vvas at hand: and many of the countrie vvent vp to Hierusalem before the Pasche to sanctifie them selues. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=56}}† They sought {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore: and they communed one vvith an other, standing in the temple, VVhat thinke you, in that he is not come to the festiual day? And the cheefe Priests & Pharisees had giuen commaundement, that if any man should knovv vvhere he vvas, he should tel, that they might apprehend him.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XI.}}}}

''51. Being the high Priest.''] Maruel not that Christ preserueth his truth in the Church as wel by the vnworthy as the worthy Prelates thereof: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The priuilege of the office & order, though in a wicked person.}}the giftes of the Holy Ghost folowing their Order and office, as we see here in Caiphas, and not their merites or person. And if this man being many waies wicked, and in part an vsurper, and the Law and Priesthod being to decline and to giue place to Christs new ordinance, had yet some assistance of God for vtterance of truth which him self meant not, nor knew not: how much more may we be assured, that Christ wil not leaue Peters Seate, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 22, 32.''}}whose faith he promised should neuer faile, though the persons which occupie the same, were as il as the blasphemous and malitious mouthes of Heretikes do affirme?

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The}} 4 part. {{sc|The}} 4 Pasche, & holy weeke of his Passion in Hierusalem.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XII.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Rulers dealing as if he hid him self, 1 he commeth to Bethania, 3 Where by occasion of Iudas the theefe murmuring at Marie Magdalens costly deuotion, he foretelleth his death. 12 From thence, though they did novv intend to kil Lazarus also, he rideth openly into Hierusalem, the people (because he had raised Lazarus) confessing with their acclamations that he is Christ. 20 Where certaine Gentils desiring to see him, 23 he foretelleth the conuersion of the vvhole vvorld from the Diuel to him, to be novv instant, as the effect of his death vpon the Crosse. 28 The Father also ansvvering from heauen to his prayer made to that purpose, 37 yet after al this, the Ievves continevv incredulous as Esay prophecied of them: 42 though many beleeued, but vvere ashamed to confesse him. 44 Wherevpon he shevveth that it is glorious before God, and saluation to them selues, to beleeue in him, and confesse him: and damnable, to despise him.''}} {{dropinitial|I|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial I, two horned animals.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=12|verse=1}}}}ESVS {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 6. Mar. 14, 3.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Munday in Holy weeke.}}therfore sixe daies before the Pasche came to Bethánia, vvhere Lazarus vvas, that had been dead, vvhom {{sc|Iesvs}} raised. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=2}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ PALME SVNDAY eue.}}∷ And they made him a supper there: and Martha ministred, but Lazarus vvas one of them that sate at the table vvith him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=3}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Of this womans extraordinarie offices of deuotion, & how acceptable they were to Christ, see the Annot.
